ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is trapezoid QRST, QR is the upper base, TS is the lower base; P is on the left side QT, M is on the right side RS, line segment PM horizontally connects the two legs, and is parallel to the two bases. Reasoning: The problem gives that M and P are the midpoints of the two legs, so PM is the midline of the trapezoid. According to the trapezoid midline theorem, the length of the midline is equal to the average of the lengths of the two bases: PM = (QR + TS)/2. Substitute TS = 2x, QR = 6x, PM = 20, obtaining 20 = (6x + 2x)/2 = 8x/2 = 4x. Therefore x = 5.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as trapezoid QRST with QR as the top base, TS as the bottom base, and segment PM drawn between the two legs QT and RS, parallel to the bases. From the text, M and P are midpoints of the legs, TS = 2x, PM = 20, and QR = 6x. Use the trapezoid midsegment theorem: the segment joining the midpoints of the legs has length equal to the average of the two bases. Set PM = (QR + TS)/2, so 20 = (6x + 2x)/2 = 4x, giving x = 5.
